text:
Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") is now on Hugging Face, and its cybersecurity results stand out. 🛡️

It's a multimodal, multilingual Mixture-of-Experts model:
🔹 ~1T total parameters, ~49B active per token
🔹 1M token context window
🔹 Text + image input, text output
🔹 Open weights under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (an MIT derivative with limits on model-as-a-service offerings)

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝘆𝗯𝗲𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿
On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index task where a model must reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it, Mistral Large 4 scores 82%. According to Mistral, several closed frontier models score near zero on this test because they refuse to attempt it.

For defenders, that gap is significant. You usually can't fix a vulnerability without first reproducing it, and legitimate incident response work often looks like an attack to a provider's content filter. Open weights also mean an API outage or policy change can't cut off your security team in the middle of an incident.

The model still declines harmful requests. On cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is the highest of any open-weight model.

𝗕𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗵𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀
📊 93% on Cybench (40 security competition challenges)
📊 93.3% attack resistance on Lakera's B3 prompt-injection benchmark
📊 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, and a 49.8% Coding Agent Index score that places it ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max
📊 Fifth-best open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗼𝗱
The model uses two kinds of sparsity together. A router picks 4 of 128 experts for each token, plus one shared expert that always runs. A DeepSeek-style sparse attention indexer picks up to 2,048 earlier positions for each query to attend to. Images go through a 1.6B Pixtral vision encoder.

𝗗𝗮𝘆-𝟬 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗯𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗱
✅ Transformers, vLLM (with a DSpark drafter for speculative decoding) and llama.cpp
✅ GGUF quants: the 2-bit version runs on a single 512 GB Apple Silicon Ultra machine
✅ LoRA fine-tuning with TRL
✅ One-command deployment on Inference Endpoints (~65 tok/s for a single request on 8×H200) and Dell Enterprise Hub

What interests me most is what this makes possible downstream. Reproduce-then-patch tasks have a verifiable reward, so they fit naturally into RL environments. Teams could distill Large 4's patching traces into smaller security models that are tuned to their own codebase, crash logs and malware samples, and that run entirely on their own infrastructure.

Are you exploring open-weight models for security work? I'd love to hear how you're approaching it. 👇

#AI #Cybersecurity #OpenSource #LLM #MachineLearning #HuggingFace #MistralAI

---

The article is internally inconsistent on the active parameter count. The text says ~49B, but the model ID is `Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`, which suggests ~52B. I used 49B to match the article's prose, but you may want to check this before posting.
